samples.summary: Non-production cookie test can pass vacuously: it only loops over `res.cookie` mock calls with no assertion that any call happened
samples.evidence: `it('sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production')` does `for (const [name,,options] of (res.cookie as jest.Mock).mock.calls) { ... }` with no `expect(res.cookie).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` — unlike its production sibling at line 540, which does assert the count. If `controller.refresh` ever stopped setting cookies (e.g. the refresh cookie name drifted so `req.cookies[refreshCookieName()]` misses and the handler throws/returns early), the loop body never executes and the test still passes green. This is the only place the bare (unprefixed) `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` naming on the *write* path is asserted. The same shape recurs in `it('never sets SameSite=None on auth cookies')` at line 576, which iterates the concatenated cookie+clearCookie calls with no length assertion.

samples.summary: No test asserts the login-URL file is owner-only (0o600), the security property the new headless branch is built on
samples.evidence: `announceLoginUrl` writes the authorization URL — which carries this login's nonce and PKCE challenge — to `login-url.txt` with `{ mode: 0o600 }`, and prints "(readable only by you)". `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` asserts only that the path is printed, that the content equals the URL, and that the file is deleted; nothing calls `statSync` on it. The repo already has this exact assertion for the session file (`packages/cli/test/session.test.ts:70-75`, `stats.mode & 0o777 === 0o600`), so the precedent exists. The `rmSync(file, {force:true})` before write — added specifically so a pre-existing world-readable file does not keep its permissions — is likewise untested: pre-creating a 0o644 file and re-running would be the guard, and nothing does that.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s TTY branch and its write-failure fallback are both untested
samples.evidence: The new helper has three branches: TTY (prints the secret-carrying URL to stderr), non-TTY success (writes the 0600 file), and non-TTY failure (prints the "could not open a browser" advice and returns undefined). Under vitest `process.stderr.isTTY` is false, so only the middle branch is exercised (login-callback.test.ts asserts `notices.some(n => n.includes(urlPath))` and that no notice contains `nonce=`). Nothing stubs `process.stderr.isTTY = true` to prove the interactive branch actually prints the URL, and nothing makes `writeFileSync`/`mkdirSync` throw to prove the fallback message is emitted and no path is returned (so no stale `rmSync` on undefined).

samples.summary: The five new `command: commandPath(this)` wiring sites (files upload/download, docs/notes/slides import) have no test — dropping any of them regresses attribution silently
samples.evidence: The diff adds `command: commandPath(this)` to `runFilesUpload`, `runFilesDownload`, `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport` and `runSlidesImport` call sites. Tests only cover the shared builders with a hand-passed string (`output.test.ts:356` `errorEnvelope(..., 'docs.import')`, `upstreamErrorJson(..., 'docs.content')`) and the commander-driven path for other commands (`docs.get`, `sheets.cells.get`, `ctx.switch`, `schema`, `docs.content`). Grepping the cli test tree for `command: 'files.upload'|'files.download'|'docs.import'|'notes.import'|'slides.import'` as an *asserted envelope field* returns nothing — only `output.test.ts:362` which passes the literal in directly. Removing the wiring line in any of the five actions leaves the whole suite green.

samples.summary: `expect(CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS).toBe(5 * 60 * 1000)` restates the constant it imports; it cannot detect the drift its comment claims to pin
samples.evidence: The test comment says "The server's budget: `STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` and the `CliAuthStore` state entry both expire at five minutes. The two ends must agree." — but the assertion compares the CLI's own exported constant against a literal in the same file. Nothing imports or otherwise references the backend's `CLI_STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` (it lives in `packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:136` and is not even exported), so if the backend shortened its window to 2 minutes this assertion would still pass. The fake-timer half of the test (advance 60s, then the full timeout) is meaningful; only the literal-equality line is self-referential.

samples.summary: The new session-cookie-name assertions do not pin `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`/`COOKIE_SECURE`, so ambient config — not the code — can decide them
samples.evidence: `it('prefixes the session cookies with the same rule')` (and the pre-existing `cookie naming` cases above it) set only `process.env.NODE_ENV`, while `isSecureCookie()` now reads `COOKIE_SECURE` and `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` *ahead of* `NODE_ENV`. Every other spec touched in this diff adds `delete process.env.GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` in `beforeEach` for exactly this reason and says so in a comment (auth.controller.spec.ts:495, cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:29, github-auth.guard.spec.ts:94). Here the `afterEach` restores those vars but nothing clears them first, so with an ambient `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://...` the `__Host-` assertions fail and with `https://...` the bare-name assertions fail — the result is decided outside the behavior under test.

samples.summary: Nothing proves the pino `req` serializer actually calls `logSafeUrl`; the redaction could be un-wired with the suite green
samples.evidence: `logSafeUrl` has a thorough unit spec, but the only consumer is the one-line `url: logSafeUrl(req.url)` inside the `LoggerModule.forRoot` serializer in `app.module.ts`. Grepping the repo for `logSafeUrl` finds only the module, the implementation and its own spec — there is no app.module test (Glob `packages/backend/src/**/app.module*` returns just the source file), so reverting the serializer to `url: req.url` would leave every test passing while every `/auth` query string goes back into the access log. Extracting the serializer object (or asserting the configured serializer) would close it.

samples.summary: `cliConfirmToken`'s nonce binding and its length-prefix anti-ambiguity claim are untested
samples.evidence: The token signs `port`, `nonce` and `challenge`. The spec covers replay against another `port` (line 161) and another `challenge` (line 174), but there is no case where only the `nonce` differs, so a token computed without the nonce part (or with the nonce dropped from `parts`) would still pass the whole suite. The doc comment also states the length prefixes exist so no re-cut of the values collides (`"9|87,6"` vs `"98|7,6"`) — no test asserts two distinct parameter triples produce distinct tokens, so removing the `${part.length}:` prefixing is likewise invisible to the suite.

samples.summary: Frontend test asserts a message for `login_state`, an error code no backend path emits — coverage of an unreachable input dressed as a regression guard
samples.evidence: The new `it.each(["oauth_state", "login_state"])` case, and the `LOGIN_ERRORS` map entry it exercises, rest on the comment "the two names for the same refusal have both been in the callback's vocabulary". Grepping the backend for `login_state` finds nothing: `auth.controller.ts:149` and `:167` both redirect to `loginErrorUrl('oauth_state')`, and no other producer exists. So half this parameterised test asserts behavior for a code that cannot arrive, while the genuinely reachable unknown-code path is already covered by the generic-message case. Not a false pass for `oauth_state`, but the added coverage is inert.

samples.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE`'s negative and numeric spellings are untested in the module that parses them
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` accepts `'true'|'1'` → true and `'false'|'0'` → false, with trimming and case-folding. The new `useSecureCookies` describe only covers `COOKIE_SECURE='true'` (line 146). Nothing in this spec covers `'false'` (the branch that must override an https callback URL), `'1'`, `'0'`, or the trim/lowercase handling; the `'false'` case is only reached indirectly through the guard spec's refusal/warning tests, which would not distinguish it from the variable being ignored entirely for a non-`https` URL.

samples.summary: `keeps the bare names for expiry` asserts an exported constant against a literal copy of itself
samples.evidence: `expect(UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES).toEqual(['wafflebase_session','wafflebase_refresh'])` restates the module's own definition (`oauth-state.ts:104-107`) and exercises no behavior. The behavior that matters — that logout reaches those names — is covered separately by `sign-out expires every cookie shape` in auth.controller.spec.ts, so this case adds no failure mode.

`baseCookieOptions()` (auth.controller.ts) constructs the object literally with `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`, `path` and never a `domain` key on any branch, so this assertion is a tautology for the object it is given. Harmless as a future-proofing marker, but it is not evidence of the `__Host-` requirement it is placed to document.
